newsitem.title: UK: Novopharm says generic Zantac on sale now.
newsitem.headline: Novopharm says generic Zantac on sale now.

text.p: Privately-owned Canadian generic drug company Novopharm Ltd said on Monday supplies of a generic version of Glaxo Wellcome Plc's ulcer drug Zantac had gone on immediate sale in parts of the U.S.

A company spokesman told Reuters that following Novopharm's agreement with rival generic manufacturer Genpharm Inc, owned by Germany's Merck KGgA, the generic drug was "on sale today in certain places."

In a statement, Novopharm chairman and chief executive officer Leslie Dan said "we signed this agreement so there could be a generic available immediately. To do anything else would have been a complete travesty, after all we have endured over the last six years to bring this product to the pharmacy shelves."

Novopharm and Genpharm agreed to bury their differences after a lengthy legal wrangle, which left Genpharm with exclusive rights to sell the drug but unable to make it because of a separate patent dispute with Glaxo Wellcome.

Novopharm, which had paid Glaxo Wellcome $70 million to market the drug two weeks ahead of Zantac's July 25 patent expiry, was stopped from selling its version following a legal challenge on July 9 by Novartis U.S. unit Geneva Pharmaceuticals Inc.
Industry sources told Reuters that the situation was still clouded and the agreement between Novopharm and Genpharm could face further legal hurdles.
